data.narrative:
Cylib is a Series A-stage climate and energy technology company founded by Lilian Schwich, Gideon Schwich, and Paul Sabarny. The target operates within a sector represented by 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Linz AG, ticker LNZA), though a sufficiently narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier does not exist to support traditional multiples-based analysis.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the company's total raised base of €140M (comprising €55M Series A capital, €26.1M NRW grant, and €63.4M BMWE grant). This approach yields an implied valuation of $280M. The peer-median approach was deemed not applicable due to insufficient comparable granularity; while 8 climate and energy peers exist in the dataset, none meet simultaneous filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar valuation tier needed to establish a reliable median.

The triangulated range is $238M to $322M, with a median of $280M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty around stage-appropriate multiples, which can vary substantially depending on technology risk, funding environment, and capital efficiency. The abundance of non-dilutive grants (€89.5M of the €140M total) introduces additional complexity in interpreting implied post-money valuation relative to equity raised. Further validation would require either expanded peer comparables or detailed revenue/growth trajectory data not present in current inputs.
